title: KV cache pre-seed + weighted routing simulation notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures notes from a small-scale simulation and a proposed runbook for region-level routing using a combination of: pre-seeding KV caches in warm-standby clusters, progressive weighted DNS/route53 shifts, and a health-weighted selector for read/write traffic. Goal: reduce user-visible tail latency and cold-start error spikes during a single-region outage while avoiding large cache stampedes in the target region.

Context / why: 
- We observed increased tail latency and transient 5xxs during the last AUS->US failover test (Q4 dry run). Root cause: cold KV cache in the failover region plus aggressive routing shift (100% in <2m) that overloaded challenger nodes.
- Existing docs handle DNS TTL and simple weighted shifts but don't cover pre-populating token-level KV cache or how to coordinate KV warmup with gradual routing.

Simulation summary (Feb 10 - Feb 14):
- Setup: two regions (us-west-2 primary, eu-west-1 standby). Standby cluster was configured identical to prod but traffic-only client LB attached for simulation.
- Workload: synthetic production-like chat/generation traffic recreated from anonymized traces (sequence length distribution preserved).
- Pre-seed approach: replay of recent warm prefixes (48h sliding window) to standby KV cache gateway 30m before any shift. We also warmed attention caches by replaying sample contexts for largest 50 templates.
- Routing policy tested: staged weighted routing (10%, 30%, 60%, 100) with 3-minute steady-state between steps. Health-aware rollback if error rate > 1% over 1-minute window or P95 latency > 1.8x baseline.

Key observations: 
- Pre-seeding reduced initial P95 latency spike by ~45% compared to cold-standby baseline. P50 unaffected as expected.
- The 3-minute ramp was generally safe; however a small surge in KV lookup latency appeared at the 60% step in one run due to an inefficient batch size setting in the standby inference runtime.
- Failure mode: if the pre-seed did not include the longest recent contexts (edge-case long conversations), requests that depended on longer cached KV prefixes still incurred work proportional to sequence length, causing token compute bursts. Mitigation: ensure pre-seed window includes high-length tail.
- DNS TTL: using a 30s TTL allowed near-immediate rollback during experiments; however external resolvers sometimes cached longer, causing a small fraction (~0.5%) of traffic to continue hitting primary after rollback. Not critical but notable.

Proposed runbook (draft) - step-by-step for region-level shift using pre-seed + weighted routing:
Preconditions (owner: SRE on-call):
- Confirm standby cluster healthy: instance counts, GPU temps, runtime process up, storage mounted, KMS accessible.
- Confirm preseed job has completed with success status and payload size within expected bounds.
- Confirm monitoring alerting thresholds configured for this shift run (error rate, P95, KV lookup latency).
- Notify stakeholders in #sre-oncall and #platform-ops channels with expected timeline and rollback criteria.

Execution steps:
1) Start pre-seed job (script: infra/scripts/preseed-kv.sh). Kick off as separate user to avoid token contamination. Record job id.
- Expected time: 20-60 minutes depending on window length.
2) Verify pre-seed completion and sample integrity: run quick verification queries (5 golden requests that should hit KV warm prefixes). Confirm responses match baseline.
3) Lower DNS TTL for affected domain to 30s if not already. Propagate change via route53 - ensure change id returned.
4) Begin weighted routing: set weights to 10% to standby. Start 3m timer.
5) Continuous monitoring during each weight step (10%, 30%, 60%, 100):
- Metrics to watch: error rate (5xx), P95 latency (overall and per-step), KV lookup latency histogram, GPU utilization, queue length, CPU steal.
- Run synthetic smoke requests every 15s (test-keys) and fail fast if mismatch or 5xx.
6) If metrics breach rollback thresholds (error rate > 1% sustained for 60s OR P95 > 1.8x baseline sustained for 60s OR KV lookup latency > 2x baseline) then:
- Immediately set routing weight back to previous step (e.g., from 60% -> 30%) and hold for 5 minutes.
- If rollback to previous step does not stabilize within 5m, set weight to 0% and restore primary-only routing.
7) After reaching 100%, hold for 10 minutes, then validate higher-level integrations (billing proxy, observability ingestion) and watch for background regression signals (quality eval drop, rerank divergence).
8) Post-shift: gradually re-increase DNS TTL to standard (300s) over 30m once stable and stakeholders ack.

Runbook tooling & automations (TODOs):
- preseed-kv.sh needs an option to prioritize high-length contexts and an option to limit replay to templates with >X usage in last N hours. (assigned: Diego)
- Add a synthetic request harness that simulates long-context requests (owner: Chen).
- Automate weight rollback via route-controller API to avoid manual console work (owner: Liam).

Known limitations and risk notes: 
- External DNS resolvers may not respect our short TTL; clients behind aggressive caches can keep hitting old endpoints. To mitigate: use in-band versioning header that allows the application to detect stale routing and trigger client-level backoff if necessary.
- Pre-seed job size vs. network egress: large pre-seed windows may push network egress and storage IOPS. Need a cost limit. Consider prioritized subset instead of full window.
- State consistency for pinned model versions: ensure standby models are same version & tokenizer. Small differences can cause downstream eval regressions.

Metrics & success criteria for a safe shift: (targets to bake into automation)
- Rolling 1m error rate <= 0.5% during shift steps (soft), hard threshold 1% for automated rollback.
- P95 latency deviation <= 1.5x baseline during majority of shift.
- KV cache hit ratio on first-hour post-shift >= 70% for the 48h preseed window.
- No more than 1% of requests receiving stale responses due to DNS caching after rollback.

Postmortem action items (from sim runs):
- Tune standby inference batch sizing to match primary throughput; add auto-scaling policy that considers KV cache warmness signals (assigned: eng-serving-runtime).
- Improve pre-seed scheduler to do prioritized warmups (highest-rank templates + long-context examples) (assigned: SRE infra).
- Add a runbook step to call out stakeholders in APAC region for cross-region shifts that affect that user base (assigned: oncall runbook owner).

Open questions / discussion points: 
- How large a time window should pre-seed cover by default? 24h vs 48h vs 7d tradeoffs discussed. Need cost/benefit data.
- Should we attempt to pre-seed KV incrementally during normal operation (background low-priority job) to keep standby "warm enough"? Pros/cons: lower shift time vs added steady-state cost.
- Which model families benefit most from pre-seed? Short generative models vs long-context transformer variants. Need classification.

Notes to self (rough):
- During one run we observed a 1.2x increase in GPU mem pressure at 60% weight; double-check tensor cache eviction heuristics.
- Ensure runbook includes Slack templates and exact route53 CLI commands for reproducibility.
- Keep a small rescue runbook for manual client-side mitigation: instruct clients to flush resolver cache when possible or to honor version header.

Appendix: quick commands and references
- preseed kick: infra/scripts/preseed-kv.sh --window 48h --prio-long --dry-run
- route weight set (internal): platform-tools routectl set-weight --service api --region eu-west-1 --weight 10
- rollback pattern: routectl set-weight --service api --region eu-west-1 --weight 0; notify #sre-oncall

Draft status: handwritten simulation notes converted to doc. Need to validate thresholds with product and serving-runtime, get sign-off, then move to in_review.

If you were running this test: checklist at top and then tape-record earliest 2 failures carefully with stack traces and sample request ids.

-- Aisha
